step_by_step_reasoning:
1. Identified system entry point DEVELOPERS (UserCompanyDeveloper) accessing the portal via ALB without needing a VPN.
2. Identified ALB routing incoming web traffic to the frontend EKS portal cluster.
3. Captured the EKS portal decoupling job requests by placing them onto an SQS queue.
4. Mapped SQS triggering execution jobs on a secondary EKS worker cluster running Terraform configurations.
5. Identified the Terraform runner EKS cluster provisioning RDS databases and VPC subnet configurations across 150 target AWS accounts.
6. Incorporated RAM (Resource Access Manager) as the management mechanism sharing standardized subnet configurations across all 150 accounts.

graph.name: Xero Developer Self-Service Infrastructure Provisioning Platform
graph.notes: Architecture showing how Xero enables 1,600+ developers to securely and rapidly provision compliant AWS infrastructure (RDS, subnets) across 150 accounts using EKS, SQS, Terraform, and Resource Access Manager (RAM).

nodes.name: DEVELOPERS
nodes.notes: 1,600+ developers accessing the internal self-service platform portal without VPN.

nodes.name: ALB
nodes.notes: Application Load Balancer providing secure external endpoint for developers.

nodes.name: EKS (Portal)
nodes.notes: Frontend Kubernetes cluster hosting self-service forms and web UI.

nodes.name: SQS
nodes.notes: Queue used to decouple portal request submissions from provisioning execution.

nodes.name: TERRAFORM
nodes.notes: Terraform configuration templates containing Xero security and compliance standards.

nodes.name: EKS (Terraform Runner)
nodes.notes: Worker Kubernetes cluster executing automated Terraform provisioning tasks.

nodes.name: SUBNET
nodes.notes: Network subnets configured across 150 target AWS accounts.

nodes.name: RAM
nodes.notes: Resource Access Manager used to share unified subnet configurations across accounts.

nodes.name: RDS
nodes.notes: Relational Database Service instances provisioned in target subnets.

edges.notes: Developers access the portal UI directly via ALB without VPN.
ALB forwards web traffic to the portal container on EKS.
Portal pushes provisioning request jobs into SQS.
SQS triggers execution of pending jobs on the Terraform runner EKS cluster.
Terraform configuration is loaded into the runner EKS pod.
Terraform runner provisions RDS database instances in target accounts.
Terraform runner configures networking and subnets across 150 AWS accounts.
RAM manages and shares single subnet configurations across all 150 accounts.
